player.name: Alex Moreno
player.level: Intermediate, plays three times a week

diego.name: Diego Álvarez

entries.title: Lesson 1 with Marta
entries.memo: Okay, notes for Alex. Good session. The volleys are the strength, fast hands, good reflexes at the net. The bandeja is the problem: when the ball gets behind his shoulder he still hits it and it goes long, we counted six long in the last drill. He changes the grip late. On defence he stands right against the back glass, so every ball off the wall jams him. Next games: bandeja cross-court and deep, not for winners, one step off the back wall, and a split step every time the other side hits. Next time we do wall exits and bandeja under pressure.

worked_on: Bandeja from the back of the service box
observed: Bandeja goes long when the ball is behind the shoulder: six long in the last drill
Volleys are the strength: fast hands at the net
Stands against the back glass on defence, so balls off the wall jam him
focus: Bandeja cross-court and deep. It is a holding shot, not a winner.
On defence, start one step further from the back glass.
Split step every time the opponents hit.
drills: 20 bandejas cross-court to a target near the side glass
Back-wall exits with a feed, 3 sets of 10
note.next: Back-wall exits, and the bandeja under pressure.

entries.title: Match: lost 4-6, 3-6
entries.text: Doubles at the club. Lost 4-6, 3-6. The bandeja went long at least six times again, mostly in the second set when I was tired. Forgot the split step completely in the second set. My partner said I never called the lobs, so we both went for two and both left one.

Point 2, 0:31: stands against the back glass; the ball off the wall jams the backhand

themes.defence: seen on video: against the glass

entries.title: Lesson 2 with Marta
entries.memo: Watched Alex's clip before the lesson, really useful. The bandeja problem is footwork, not the arm: he turns sideways too late so the contact is behind him. We fixed it by turning as soon as he sees the lob. Wall exits much better, he is off the glass now. His partner's point about calling is right, I want that in the notes. Focus: turn sideways early, call mine or yours on every lob, and keep the split step.

observed: The clip showed the cause: turning sideways too late puts the contact behind the head
With an early turn, most bandejas landed deep
Wall exits much better: he now starts off the glass
focus: Turn sideways as soon as you see the lob.
Keep the split step, especially in the second set.
drills: Shadow the early turn: 3 sets of 15 without a ball

entries.title: Match: won 6-4, 7-5
entries.text: Won 6-4, 7-5. The early turn works, the bandeja stayed deep most of the time. Called most lobs. When they pushed us back my lobs were short and they smashed them. Played much better at the net.

entries.title: Briefing for Diego, before Lisbon
entries.text: Two lessons with Marta in London, two matches since. Strength: volleys at the net. Fixed in lessons and now holding in matches: bandeja depth, after an early sideways turn. Working on: calling the ball, split step when tired. New from the last match: lobs are short when pushed back, and opponents smash them. Alex reports playing better in lessons than in games. Suggested focus: lob depth from defence.

entries.title: Lesson 3 with Diego, in Lisbon
entries.memo: Read the briefing, that saved us the first fifteen minutes. The lob is short because he lobs with his arm, not his legs, so under pressure there is nothing behind it. We worked on low, deep lobs from the back wall using the legs. Another thing Marta may not have seen: after a good lob he waits at the back instead of going to the net with his partner. He also uses the víbora on balls that are too low, I would keep it for high balls on the forehand side.

worked_on: Lobs from the back wall, with the legs
Going to the net together after a lob
observed: The lob is short because it comes from the arm; with the legs it reaches the back third
After a good lob he stays back instead of taking the net with his partner
Uses the víbora on balls that are too low
focus: Lob with your legs, finish tall.
After a good lob, go to the net with your partner.
Keep the víbora for high balls on the forehand side.
drills: Lob from a feed off the back wall, 4 sets of 8
Lob then move to the net together, 10 minutes
note.next: The transition to the net after a lob.

themes.transition: new: stays back after a good lob

entries.title: Social game in Lisbon
entries.text: Social game with locals. Lobs deeper, the legs thing works. Still stayed back after lobbing a few times, my partner went up alone twice.

entries.title: Lesson 4 with Inés, back in London
entries.memo: First lesson with Alex. The briefing was great, I knew exactly where he was with three coaches' notes in two minutes. Confirmed the lob is better. We worked on the transition, moving up together after the lob. One more thing: his racket is heavy for how he swings, he could try a lighter, rounder one. I have no stake in which one, I only suggested he demo a couple.

worked_on: Moving to the net together after a lob
observed: Lob depth confirmed, from the legs
Transition: moves up late, but together when prompted
The racket looks heavy for his swing
focus: After the lob, count one and move up with your partner.
Try demo rackets: lighter, rounder shape.
drills: Lob, move, volley: 3 sets of 10 points
note.next: Back with Marta: full points, pressure on the bandeja and the lob together.

entries.disclosure: The coach states she has no commercial interest in the racket suggestion.

entries.title: Briefing for Marta, next lesson
entries.text: Since your two lessons: one lesson with Diego in Lisbon and one with Inés in London, two more games. Bandeja: holding deep in matches after your early-turn fix. New since you: lobs were short because they came from the arm; Diego fixed it with the legs and Inés confirmed it. Open: going to the net together after a lob, worked on by Diego and Inés, still inconsistent in games. Diego suggests keeping the víbora for high forehand balls. Inés suggested a lighter racket and declared no interest. Suggested plan: full points that combine the bandeja and the lob under pressure.
